content.comment_body: Hello everyone, hope you are well! I have a question regarding [product_name] and [product_name]. Is it possible to configure a [company_name] PLC and an HMI so they communicate using just one IP address? Currently, each device—[company_name] PLC and HMI—has its own IP address, but we are trying to set them up to use a single IP address. We keep ending up with two separate IP addresses for both devices. How can we set this communication up to use only one IP address? Thanks for any help.

I'm not sure I follow your question. Every device on an Ethernet network needs its own unique IP address to be identified and communicate properly. [product_name] and HMI must each have different IP addresses.

Hi! Both [product_name] and HMI have their own IP addresses. We're using Modbus TCP to monitor these devices. The problem is that we don't have enough available IP addresses to assign to each device, so I'm wondering if it's possible to configure the system so they can communicate using a single IP address? Any advice is welcome, thank you.
It seems there may be some misunderstanding. On Ethernet networks, it isn't possible for two devices to share the same IP address. Both [product_name] and HMI must have distinct IP addresses.

It sounds like the IP address limits are being set by site requirements. Keep in mind that Modbus TCP devices or other field instruments might be on a different network. It's worth discussing the network layout with whoever handles the site's infrastructure. Alternatively, you could use a network switch that restricts access, connecting only the PLC to the field devices while blocking outside network connections. This way, you can assign IP addresses that fit your needs, even if they're outside the usual range.
Another option is to use a gateway device to bridge two subnets.
Hi, Yes, you're correct—the site's setup is dictating the available IP addresses. Thank you for your helpful advice, it's much appreciated. Thanks.

analysis.insight_summary: The original poster has limited IP addresses available on site and is unsure about network requirements for configuring communication between a [product_name] and an HMI. There is confusion about whether a single IP address can be used by both devices. Experienced contributors explain that each device on an Ethernet network must have a unique IP address, highlighting a basic gap in networking knowledge versus device configuration options.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to configure both [product_name] and HMI to communicate over the network using only one IP address, due to site constraints on IP availability.
